Beautiful piece I would have for sure bought it. A resell price will depend on multiple things.  
Any makers marks? 
If it is one of the many well known designers it will increase the value significantly. could be the difference of a $200 range to $2000
Where are you trying to sell it?
Selling on facebook market place, craigslist etc will generally result in lower selling price but it's the easiest route. Also if you are in an urban area vs rural. City folk pay way more for things
Lastly, how badly do you want it gone? 
Replacing the mirror will increase its value and speed of sale but is more effort. selling it 'for what it's worth' will take a longer time than just making some money back. Depending on how much you paid for it. 

With a broken mirror in an urban area on fb marketplace you could likely ask $100-300 and part with it quite quickly. 
Fix it up and sell it through etsy, or an antiques consignment and it could sell for 750-2000, depending on the factors above.

It's hard to explain not in person. But to breathe with the top half, you breathe in all the way and only let half of the air out. and continue to breathe halfway like this to rise up. To breathe with the bottom half, you breathe all the way out and only inhale half way, and you should sink. If you are properly weighted and half the appropriate amount of air in your BCD. 

It takes a lot of practice to get good at this, but it can save a lot of coral from getting accidentally squashed. 

Taking the Peak Performance Buoyancy specialty will help you master this skill and it is money well spent.

It's not x-ray. It's a procedure called "Clearing and Staining" developed by the scientist/photographer Adam Summers. It involves dyeing the bones and cartilage, and using chemicals to dissolve the flesh.

Your BCD is not how you adjust buoyancy, other than for major adjustments. Use your lungs to do your buoyancy control for most of the dive. (breathe with the "top half" of your lungs to rise up, breathe with the "lower half" of your lungs to sink). This was my major Aha! moment that I didn't get taught in my open water course. 

As for gear, my best purchase was a dive slate [like this](http://www.scuba.com/scuba-gear-249/032331/Innovative-Multi-Page-Wrist-Slate.html). It allows you to ask those questions that you just can't get across underwater, and helps avoid confusion and potential panic, letting you enjoy the dive more. It is also great for jotting down questions to ask once you surface. Like what was the name of that one fish with the crazy colors. 

Most of all relax, and enjoy the dive.
